Implement via (a) cuBLAS/CUTLASS GEMM of a ones-vector against the one-hot matrix, or (b) WMMA/mma.sync tensor-core accumulation of one-hot fragments, or (c) bmm over chunked one-hot. ROOT CAUSE (SASS-confirmed): __vseteq4/__vcmpeq4 each compile to ~5 LOP3/SHF (no HW byte-eq), and the WMMA fragment layout forces 32 lanes x 4 SIMD-compares to classify only 16 bytes/MMA = ~30-40 ALU ops/byte vs the atomic kernel's ~1-2 ops/byte. So building the one-hot to FEED the tensor cores costs ~20x more ALU than the smem atomics it replaces -- tensor cores sit at the SAME 76% but the ALU saturates first. The 16x16 output is too small for any int8 MMA tile to amortize (raw m16n8k32 is WORSE: 2 MMAs/16x16 each need own B -> more compares/byte). RECOMMENDATION: do NOT spend more briefs on tensor-core/one-hot histogram -- it is a thorough negative; the one-hot construction ALU cost is a hard structural floor ~25-30us, 2.5-3x off the atomic frontier. The histogram is genuinely walled near ~10us by EITHER atomic serialization (champion) OR one-hot ALU (this). If any histogram brief remains, it should be w1's patient remote micro-tuning of the R=32 atomic champion toward #1's 10.218 (a <5% gap, micro-structure) -- the orthogonal algorithm classes (tensor, warp-vote, sort, global-atomic) are now ALL closed. it1 conflict-aware RBIG=8 bin-major replication (hist_stage1_repl, BIG bracket only). FALSIFIES replication as conflict lever: ncu 10.5M c10 atomic-conflicts 672462(R1)->632508(R8) = only 6pct cut (NOT 4x predicted) + 66304 new ld-conflicts from 8-way merge = 698812 total WORSE; shape5 13.944us vs ~12.96 baseline; geomean 10.337 vs 10.262. CORRECT on 10.5M (probe+benchmark check:pass). Root cause: bank=(bin*RBIG+lane%RBIG)%32; for R=8 the bin*8%32 term takes only 4 values {0,8,16,24} so cold bins span just 4 bank-groups -> R spreads only SAME-bin replicas (helps the hot evil-bin which HW already coalesces via same-address) NOT distinct cold bins (the real 672K conflict source). Confirms 'replication relocates atomics, never reduces conflicts'. Pivoting to register pre-accumulation to cut atomic INSTRUCTION count itself.

it2 register-cache pre-accumulation (hist_stage1_regcache K=16, BIG mode 2). CATASTROPHIC: shape5 156us (13x slower), ncu conflicts 1.96M (3x worse), atomic insts 397884 (MORE not fewer); geomean 15.398. CORRECT on 10.5M but disqualifying. TWO fundamental root causes: (1) direct-mapped tag[s]/cnt[s] dynamically indexed (s=bin&15 runtime) -> register arrays w/ non-compile-time index SPILL TO LOCAL MEM = the 13x; (2) per-lane predication does NOT remove a WARP-WIDE atomic instruction (whole warp issues if any lane misses), so a reg cache at best thins active-lane count per inst by ~contention%, never removes insts. Dynamic-index reg cache DEAD. Reset to baseline; pivoting to a bin-decorrelating swizzle/stride layout that spreads COLD bins across all 32 banks (the real conflict source).

KEY THEORY (ncu-proven, settles the whole conflict question): cold-bin conflicts are a BIRTHDAY-BOUND floor -- within one atomicAdd instruction the warp's 32 lanes write 32 i.i.d.-uniform cold bins and bank=bin%32, so ~12/32 collide => 672K. ANY scheme where >1 lane can share a bank-region keeps these collisions; the ONLY conflict-free layout for uniform data is bank=f(lane ALONE) => R=32 (smem[bin*32+lane], bank=lane). This means sibling w0's conflict-free-LAYOUT and w4's bin-XOR-SWIZZLE CANNOT reach the 329K/0 ideal for cold bins either -- proven by measurement: RBIG=8 (it1) only cut 672K->632K, RR=16 cut to 337K (exactly the birthday half), only RR=32 hits ~2K.

Trajectory cold-single-launch: naive-R32 17.6 -> cf32 11.39 -> +2blk 10.82 -> +vec-zero 10.59us (champ 12.96). ab2 faithful (cold+L2clear) shape5 B/A med 0.93->0.896->0.8489 (B ~15pct faster); all-6 geomean B/A 0.9728; smaller 5 shapes EXACT-TIE (R1 path untouched). EXACT all 5 test + probe correct=True on 10.5M.
